correctness.rationale: The all-parameter proof is elementary but complete: q constant payloads yield at most two orientation classes under a single check, forcing r_sys>=2 for q>=3; fixed (0,1) references attain 2. For unrestricted coding, exactly 3F(q-1)+3 primitive triples exist and a union bound on common prime factors gives F(m)>m^2/2, hence 3F(m)+3>q^2. Cartesian extension gives q^k codewords of length k+1 for every k>=2. The two length-two orientation classes establish the exceptional k=1 lower bound and a binary one-check encoder supplies the q=2 case. The supplied program recreates primitive representatives and equivalent classes through independent rational and gcd methods; finite runs are explicitly not substituted for general proof.

value.rationale: Systematic fixed-to-fixed Pearson coding is explicitly motivated by unknown gain/offset memories and a published two-reference construction. The result turns the question of whether two references are merely convenient into a sharp unavoidable overhead law for every alphabet size and message length. It also shows that a non-systematic encoder can save one whole symbol for every q>=3,k>=2, despite preserving the same q^k message count. This exact universal design boundary is qualitatively different from simply recomputing the known maximal Pearson-code cardinality; no downstream theorem is required.
